title: Predictions from Labeled Data
prompt: You want to use historical labels indicating whether customers churned to predict the probability of future churn. Which learning approach should you use?

choices.explanation: It uses known target labels to predict discrete classes.
It finds similar groups in unlabeled data.
It learns a policy through actions and rewards in an environment.

learning.reason: It uses known target labels to predict discrete classes.
learning.concept: For continuous targets, regression is a candidate; for categorical targets, classification is a candidate.

title: Evaluating Missed Detections
prompt: For anomaly detection, you want to reduce cases where an actual anomaly is classified as normal. Which metric directly measures the reduction of missed anomalies?

choices.explanation: If normal cases are the majority, accuracy can remain high even when many anomalies are missed.
This is the proportion of detected anomalies that are truly anomalous, and it primarily reflects false positives.
This is the proportion of actual anomalies that are detected, so it directly reflects missed anomalies.

learning.reason: Recall is the proportion of actual anomalies that are detected, so it directly reflects missed anomalies.
learning.concept: Increasing recall may also increase false positives. Consider both the operational cost of missed anomalies and the cost of false positives.

title: Answering with the Latest Documents
prompt: Because our FAQ changes daily, we want our internal chat assistant to answer with citations to the latest supporting sources. Which approach is suitable?

choices.text: Use RAG to add retrieved results and sources to the input
choices.explanation: It can retrieve current documents and provide them as supporting evidence. The model does not need to be retrained every time.
Frequent updates take effort, and the source of each citation in an answer cannot be tracked automatically.
This adjusts generation diversity but does not retrieve up-to-date information.

learning.reason: It can retrieve current documents and provide them as supporting evidence. The model does not need to be retrained every time.
learning.concept: RAG can still miss relevant documents or generate content that is not supported by the evidence. Evaluate retrieval quality and answer quality separately.

title: Reducing Toxicity
prompt: We want to reduce hate speech in the output of an internal AI system. Which control is appropriate to add to Bedrock inference?

choices.text: Change the model's on-demand pricing configuration
choices.explanation: Changing pricing or usage mode does not evaluate content.

choices.text: Use the content filters in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
choices.explanation: They can detect and control harmful content in specified categories.

choices.text: Reduce the maximum number of inference tokens
choices.explanation: This makes answers shorter but does not identify specific harmful content.

learning.reason: They can detect and control harmful content in specified categories.
learning.concept: Use guardrails as one layer of defense, and retain human evaluation as appropriate for the use case.

title: Model Bias
prompt: We want to check a hiring support model for group-specific bias that may not be visible in its overall accuracy. What is suitable?

choices.text: Look only at accuracy aggregated across all groups
choices.explanation: Errors for smaller groups can be obscured by the overall average.

choices.text: Measure response latency by group only
choices.explanation: This does not evaluate prediction errors or how they are distributed.

choices.text: Compare errors by group using appropriately partitioned evaluation data
choices.explanation: This can reveal different error patterns across groups.

learning.reason: This can reveal different error patterns across groups.
learning.concept: Set evaluation metrics and acceptable disparities based on the model's purpose, the people it affects, and the expected impact.

title: Data for Final Evaluation
prompt: For a classification model, you selected a model after reviewing the validation data repeatedly. What should you use to measure its final generalization performance?

choices.text: The same validation set used for model selection
choices.explanation: The selection process has adapted to that set, so the final evaluation may be optimistic.
This measures fit to examples the model has already learned from and is insufficient for evaluating performance on unseen data.

choices.text: A test set that was not used for selection
choices.explanation: It enables a final evaluation on data that was not affected by the selection process.

learning.reason: It enables a final evaluation on data that was not affected by the selection process.
learning.concept: Separating the roles of training, selection and tuning, and final evaluation makes it easier to detect overfitting to evaluation data.
